criteria.original_requirement: Consume Back then replace collector; second collector must not repeat it.
A load sent before first attachment is processed exactly once.
Two WebViews with one navigator are either rejected/documented or have deliberate broadcast behavior.

source_review: The common navigator now owns a bounded64-command Channel and exclusive Mutex admission, rather than replay-one broadcast. Pre-attachment loads are retained once; a received Back/Forward/Stop is never replayed to a replacement collector. Simultaneous owners are rejected explicitly and documented; all production platform consumers use this shared contract. Headers are snapshotted and detached capability flags cleared.
reused_results: 37/37 actual Linux desktop methods in seven fresh XML at734 exact own-Git inputs. The exact common tests consume pre-attachment Load+Back, replace the collector without replay, and reject a second owner; the actual native JavaFX/window repeated-stop/reattachment method also passes. This reuses the just-reviewed run; zero additional executions or repeated CI suites.
limits: Common consumer ownership/queue and real JavaFX window stop integration, not actual multi-Compose-window mount/GC certification on every backend. Android Chromium history-restoration/replacement fixture remains failed and open under BUILD-006/release-readiness; its broader native-history gate is not the original shared-flow replay contract and is not waived. Original public signatures retained; bounded overflow now fails explicitly and prior replay/broadcast behavior intentionally removed. Other physical/minimum/ownership/security/consumer/ABI/release gates remain independent.
